quote: S8.2-7: Is the object a package installed on the computer, or was it obtained as part of such a package and does it remain as received? S8.2-8: Then it is **an installed object**, whether it contains programs or not: fonts, icons, translations, lookup tables, firmware, default setting values, a package containing only dependencies. S8.2-16: What is installed is recorded by one of three lines: a line of its own; the line of the package as part of which it was obtained; a line from which the system itself built or obtained it—a compiled copy, a generated list, a package installed as a dependency of a recorded package.
decision: installed object (question 1); must be recorded; covered by the line of the package as part of which it was obtained (or by a line of its own)
note: Decided for files that remain as received; whether a given file has been changed since installation is a fact of the inventory (Section 9.2), and a changed file goes on to questions 2-4. A theme is not named in S8.2-8 but meets the condition of S8.2-7 like any other part of a package.

quote: S2.2-2: The test is removal: if, after an object is removed, the computer stops doing something or something becomes impossible on it, the object must be recorded. S2.2-4: content—documents, photographs, the contents of databases: after it is removed, the computer does and can do the same, and only the content itself is unavailable;
decision: must be recorded by S2.2-2 (after removal, showing text in that font or those icons and that theme becomes impossible) / need not be recorded by the reason of S2.2-4 (programs fall back to other fonts, icons and themes; the computer does the same and only the removed item is unavailable)
meaning_answer: Yes: it is installed (obtained with a package), so it must be in the declaration, covered by the line of that package.
achievable: Yes: covering it by the package line forbids none of the ordinary actions of Section 9.2; installing a package is already one of them and is recorded.
note: The text does not say which effects of removal count as the computer stopping doing something; a font, icon set or theme is neither in the list of S2.2-4 nor in S2.2-7 (S2.2-7 names the theme of one program only, not a theme shared by all programs).

quote: S8.2-7: Is the object a package installed on the computer, or was it obtained as part of such a package and does it remain as received? S8.2-8: Then it is **an installed object**, whether it contains programs or not: fonts, icons, translations, lookup tables, firmware, default setting values, a package containing only dependencies. S8.2-16: What is installed is recorded by one of three lines: a line of its own; the line of the package as part of which it was obtained; a line from which the system itself built or obtained it—a compiled copy, a generated list, a package installed as a dependency of a recorded package.
decision: installed object (question 1); must be recorded; by a line of its own if installed explicitly, covered by the line of the recorded package if installed as its dependency
note: Which of the two lines applies depends on the inventory fact explicit/dependency (Section 9.2); under either it must be recorded.

quote: S2.2-1: Whatever the computer’s behaviour depends on—what it does and what can be done on it—must be recorded. S2.2-2: The test is removal: if, after an object is removed, the computer stops doing something or something becomes impossible on it, the object must be recorded.
decision: undecided: removed alone, the package leaves its dependencies in place and nothing stops, so the test of S2.2-2 is not met; removed by the package manager together with its now unneeded dependencies, programs stop; no exemption of S2.2-3 to S2.2-7 names it
meaning_answer: Yes: it is an installed package, so it must be in the declaration, by a line of its own or as a dependency of a recorded package.
achievable: Yes: recording a package forbids none of the ordinary actions of Section 9.2.
note: The text does not fix how the object is removed for the test, and S2.2-2 is only a sufficient condition; whether future updates and dependency cleanup count as behaviour depending on it (S2.2-1) is not said.

quote: S8.2-9: Is the object code that the computer executes or can execute: on its own, at a person’s command, or through another program with that program’s rights? S8.2-10: Then it is a **program**, whoever wrote it and wherever it came from; a program belongs to what is installed. S8.2-16: What is installed is recorded by one of three lines: a line of its own; the line of the package as part of which it was obtained; a line from which the system itself built or obtained it—a compiled copy, a generated list, a package installed as a dependency of a recorded package.
decision: program (question 2; question 1 does not apply because the copy was built after installation, and question 4 'cache' is never reached); must be recorded; covered by the line of the code from which it was built (S8.2-16, 'a compiled copy')
note: Reading question for the author (both readings require recording, so not a gap of the failure condition; see QUESTIONS.md): S8.2-16 says 'the system itself built'; if the building program is not counted as 'the system' (e.g. a program in the home directory), the copy needs a line of its own. If the copy runs inside a recorded program and cannot launch programs or change what is installed or settings, S8.2-21 would apply, but the order of S8.2-6 keeps question 2 first.

quote: S2.2-5: cache: after it is removed, the computer does the same, only more slowly; S2.2-10: code that another program executes must be recorded if the program runs it with the program’s own rights, so that the code can do whatever the program can do: scripts executed by an interpreter (python, bash), shell startup files, an editor configuration written in the editor’s programming language.
decision: need not be recorded by S2.2-5 (after removal the program rebuilds it; the computer does the same, only more slowly) / must be recorded by S2.2-10 (it is code the program executes with its own rights)
meaning_answer: Yes, but only as derived: it must be in the declaration as covered by the line of the code it was compiled from, not by a line of its own.
achievable: Yes: covering the copy by its source line forbids none of the ordinary actions of Section 9.2; the program keeps compiling as before.
note: Neither sentence gives precedence over the other.

quote: S8.1-5: A general-purpose program with a built-in installer counts as an installer in that part of its functionality. S8.1-6: **Package**—what an installer installs and removes as a whole; in a system that is installed and updated as an image, the image is a package. S8.2-21: Code that runs inside a recorded program and cannot itself launch programs or change what is installed and the computer’s settings—a web page in a browser, a guest system in a virtual machine—need not be recorded.
decision: installed object, must be recorded by a line of its own, if the browser's extension manager is an installer (S8.1-5, S8.1-6, question 1) / need not be recorded, if it is not: then question 1 is no, question 2 is no because the extension does not run 'with that program’s rights' (it gets only the permissions the browser grants it), and S8.2-21 names exactly such code
meaning_answer: Yes: the person installed it and the browser installs and removes it as a whole, so it belongs to what is installed and must be in the declaration by a line of its own.
achievable: Yes: the browser's extension installer can add the extension to the declaration instead of forbidding the installation; how it adds is outside the definition (Section 8.5).
note: S8.1-4 makes an installer a program that installs and removes 'programs'; the text does not say whether code that runs inside another program with restricted rights counts as a program for S8.1-4. Its only test of a program (S8.2-9) points away from it, while S8.1-5 covers general-purpose programs with a built-in installer. Question 1 therefore has no fixed answer.

quote: S8.1-4: **Installer**—a program of the system whose purpose, according to its documentation, includes installing and removing programs: the system package manager, package managers of programming languages and of application packages. S8.1-6: **Package**—what an installer installs and removes as a whole; in a system that is installed and updated as an image, the image is a package. S8.2-7: Is the object a package installed on the computer, or was it obtained as part of such a package and does it remain as received?
decision: installed object (question 1: the game is what the store, an installer by S8.1-4 or S8.1-5, installs and removes as a whole); must be recorded by a line of its own (S8.2-16)
note: The game is also code (question 2), but question 1 comes first. Decided on the premise that the store's documentation states that it installs and removes games; that is a documentation fact, not a gap.

quote: S8.2-4: A command that a person typed himself or herself is that person’s action, not an object.
decision: not an object; nothing to record for the command itself
note: What the command leaves on the computer is decided separately as objects: e.g. a program it installs outside any installer is a program (S8.2-9, S8.2-10) and needs a line of its own (S8.2-16).

quote: S8.2-14: A value obeyed only by a program that a person runs for himself or herself is a setting if it launches something or grants access; otherwise it is a record of that program. S8.2-2: The rest need not be recorded. S8.2-23: A file that a program executes as code counts as code even when it contains setting values; a file that a program only reads as values does not count as code.
decision: record of that program (question 2 no by S8.2-23 for a value file; question 3 no; S8.2-14: a theme neither launches anything nor grants access); need not be recorded
note: If the value is stored in a file that the editor executes as code (e.g. an init file in the editor's language), S8.2-23 makes it code: question 2, a program, must be recorded by a line of its own. Which applies is a fact about the file, not a gap.

quote: S2.2-1: Whatever the computer’s behaviour depends on—what it does and what can be done on it—must be recorded. S2.2-2: The test is removal: if, after an object is removed, the computer stops doing something or something becomes impossible on it, the object must be recorded.
decision: must be recorded by the words of S2.2-1 (while it exists, the computer's behaviour depends on it) / not required by the test that S2.2-2 names for that rule (after removal the system creates it anew and the computer goes on doing the same; for some such objects S2.2-5 'cache' also fits)
meaning_answer: Yes, but only as derived: covered by the line of the program or setting that creates it, with no line of its own.
achievable: Yes: covering it by its creator's line forbids none of the ordinary actions of Section 9.2.
note: The text does not fix when 'after an object is removed' is observed (before or after the system creates it anew), and does not say whether an object recreated with new content (e.g. a fresh identifier or key) changes what the computer does.
